subject: Follow-up: DPA roles, subprocessors, and breach notification workflow
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap + items we said we'd follow up on (DPA roles, subprocessors, breach timeline)

Hi Elisabeth / Privacy team,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the thorough run through of MedSync's privacy bar. Quick written recap and asks so nothing gets lost:

1) Controller vs processor: you asked us to confirm whether Redwood treats customer-provided patient records as controller-managed data and what that means for logging and retention.
2) Subprocessors: you wanted a current list and the process for adding new subprocessors, plus notification timelines.
3) Breach notice: confirmation of our incident notification SLA and content (timing, root cause, affected data).
4) Evidence: you requested SOC 2 summary and encryption details (KMS/HSM) for storage in your vendor registry.

Attached is a short one-pager that maps our standard DPA language to MedSync's questions and a draft with the three small redline suggestions you mentioned.

Next steps I propose:
- Markus (privacy/legal) will answer the controller/processor and breach notice specifics in a follow-up email (by tomorrow).
- I can share SOC2 and encryption docs with your privacy-ops contact after we confirm the NDA channel.
- If the redlines look OK, we can push for a signature and start a scoped security intake.

Anything I missed or that you'd like prioritized first?

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

[Attachment: redwood-dpa-summary-2026-02-04.docx (3 pages)]
From: Elisabeth Hartman <elisabeth.hartman@medsynchealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy-ops@medsynchealth.com
Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + items we said we'd follow up on (DPA roles, subprocessors, breach timeline)

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Controller/Processor: MedSync will be the controller for patient records. We need Redwood to affirm processor status and provide details on how data segregation is enforced for multi-tenant flows. In particular: what metadata you store, and for how long.
- Subprocessors: we require 30 days' notice before a new subprocessor comes online and a runbook for how we are notified. Please confirm your current subprocessors and whether any are outside the US/EU.
- Breach notice: our legal team wants to understand your timeline for initial notification and follow-up remediation reports. 72 hours is our baseline expectation, but we are flexible if there are operational reasons; we need the runbook.

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (we will prefer that) or only Redwood-managed KMS?

I've attached the redlines from my counsel — they're light but we want explicit language around notification timing and subprocessors.

Best,
Elisabeth
VP, Regulatory Affairs | MedSync Health

[Attachment: MedSync_DPA_requested_changes.pdf (redlines, 2 pages)]
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elisabeth Hartman <elisabeth.hartman@medsynchealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + items we said we'd follow up on (DPA roles, subprocessors, breach timeline)

Hi Elisabeth — thanks for the clear notes and the redlines. I wanted to address each of the items you raised with the level of detail your counsel will need.

Controller / Processor
- Confirmation: Redwood accepts processor status for customer-provided patient records under our standard DPA language. We will not assert rights to data beyond providing the service.
- Data types logged: operational metadata we retain includes request timestamps, model selection metadata (model ID, version), and trace-level error hashes for debugging. We do not retain full prompt/response pairs beyond the retention window unless explicitly requested for debugging.
- Retention policy: default retention for request logs is 30 days; retention for minimal audit logs is 365 days. We can configure shorter retention for regulated customers via contract (we've done 90-day and 0-day customizations).

Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors: compute (CloudProviderX), logging/observability (LogStreamCo), key management (KeyVaultInc).
- Regions: all subprocessors operate in US and EU regions; none of our listed core subprocessors are based in APAC for this account.
- Process: Redwood provides 30 days' notice for material subprocessor additions and posts an updated list to a hosted registry. For critical security vendors, we provide direct notification to the customer's security contact and an opt-out mechanism during the notice period.

Breach notification and incident reports
- Initial notification: Redwood will provide an initial notification within 72 hours of confirming a security incident impacting customer data. The initial notice includes scope, impacted assets, and immediate mitigations.
- Follow-ups: detailed root cause analysis and remediation steps are provided in subsequent reports (72 hours + periodic updates until remediation).

Encryption and keys
- Key management: Redwood supports Redwood-managed KMS by default and also offers customer-managed keys (CMK) via our KeyVaultInc integration for customers that require it. We can include CMK options in the SOW.

Evidence and next steps
- I'll attach a SOC 2 summary and our KMS encryption whitepaper to this thread; Jordan will share the secure link to the SOC artifact via the NDA channel.
- We are comfortable accepting the limited redlines you sent; I will work with legal to produce a tracked-change DPA that reflects the agreed notification timelines and subprocessor notice.

If you want, we can set a short follow-up call to walk counsel through the retention options and CMK setup (15–20 minutes).

Regards,
Markus Klein
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
